content.title: About
content.content: Sweet rice cooked with honey is a dish of boiled rice sweetened with natural honey. It has a soft, slightly sticky texture and a gentle honey aroma, making it a popular dessert in Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet rice is often served in Japan (mochi) and China (gong bao).
Honey not only adds sweetness but also brings antioxidant properties.
Traditionally, rice with honey was used in rituals symbolizing prosperity and abundance.
In some regions, honey‑sweetened rice is served during New Year celebrations as a symbol of a sweet life.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides a steady release of energy thanks to its slowly digestible starches.

items.title: Natural sweetener
items.content: Honey contains enzymes, vitamins, and minerals that may support the immune system.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Easily digestible rice combined with the prebiotic properties of honey promotes a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Flavonoids in honey help combat free radicals.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: A warm bowl of honey‑sweetened rice is often enjoyed as a calming evening dessert.

items.title: Honey allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to honey, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice has a high GI, and adding honey further spikes blood sugar; people with diabetes should limit portions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption of sweet rice can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve warm as a dessert, use as a filling for pancakes, stir into yogurt, or include in breakfast bowls. Add nuts, dried fruit, or cinnamon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in a steamer or microwave with a splash of water to restore softness.
